review_scope.allowed: Internal research and CI use on NVIDIA GPU systems by the research-engine project.
not_reviewed_or_authorized: redistribution of the trusted runtime bundle as a standalone product
commercial redistribution of CUDA developer tools
distribution of audio/video codec products or services requiring separate patent licenses
review_scope.notice_preservation: Promoted runtime bundle remains byte-for-byte content-addressed and retains all bundled LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE files.

upstream.evidence: LICENSE is Apache License 2.0; pyproject declares Apache-2.0.
LICENSE is Apache License 2.0; package metadata identifies version 0.0.8 as Apache-2.0.

third_party_notices.note: Wheel also bundles license/notices for dav1d, libavif, libjpeg-turbo, libpng, libwebp, libyuv, zlib, and NVIDIA CUDA components.

upstream.evidence: TorchCodec LICENSE is BSD 3-Clause; project documentation directs CUDA-enabled users to NVIDIA CUDA license terms.

packages.package_role: NVIDIA-published 2.3 KB metapackage that contains no software and selects CUDA Toolkit component packages.

evidence: PyPI exact wheel filename/size/SHA-256 match the accepted bundle artifact.
CUDA 12.9.1 EULA grants installation and use of the SDK.
Developer tools not identified as distributable are for internal use.
CUDA Toolkit license scope is development of applications for NVIDIA GPU systems.
This review authorizes internal research/CI use only and does not authorize standalone redistribution.

rationale: The five packages missing wheel-level license metadata have exact artifact-bound or authoritative upstream terms compatible with internal, non-redistributed research/CI use. Apache-2.0 and BSD-3-Clause artifacts retain their bundled notices. NVIDIA CUDA 12.9.1 permits installation/use and internal developer-tool use on NVIDIA GPU systems; redistribution is explicitly outside this review.
